terms.meaning: a slow, salted method for scrambling passwords so they cannot be read back
a one-way scrambled form of a value, used so the original is never stored
a group of database changes that all succeed or all fail together
a temporary block on signing in after too many failed tries

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for password handling
sections.what: Brings in bcrypt for scrambling passwords, the random and hash tools, error types, configuration, the database and the revoke reason labels.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: PasswordService (part 1)
sections.title: Hashing passwords and lockout rules
sections.what: Scrambles passwords with bcrypt at twelve rounds and compares them on sign-in. Counts failed tries and locks an account for a set time once the limit is reached.
sections.why: Likely reason: a slow hash protects stored passwords, and a lockout slows down guessing.
sections.watch_out: If the lockout settings are missing, the app silently uses five tries and fifteen minutes.

sections.name: PasswordService: resetFailedAttempts
sections.title: Clearing failures and making reset tokens
sections.what: Clears failed tries after a good login. Creates a random reset token, stores only its hash, expires it after one hour, and allows three requests per hour.
sections.why: Likely reason: stored hashes mean a leaked database does not reveal usable reset tokens.
sections.watch_out: Unknown emails get no token and no error, but known accounts get a rate-limit error after three requests, which reveals that the account exists.

sections.name: PasswordService: resetPassword
sections.title: Using a reset token to set a new password
sections.what: Looks up the token by its hash, rejects used or expired tokens, sets the new password, marks the token used and revokes refresh tokens, all in one transaction.
sections.why: Likely reason: the transaction keeps the password change and token use from happening separately.
sections.watch_out: Only refresh tokens are revoked here, so access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire.

sections.name: PasswordService: if
sections.title: Changing a password while signed in
sections.what: Checks the current password, saves the new hash, and revokes refresh tokens in one transaction.
sections.why: Likely reason: changing a password should end sessions that may have a stolen password.
sections.watch_out: The code revokes every refresh token for the user, including the current device, although the comment says the current session is kept.

summary: Handles password scrambling and checking, failed-login lockouts, and password reset and change.
purpose: Keeps password logic in one place for the auth module.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The header mentions bcrypt and a timing-safe comparison, and bcrypt is used.
how: Passwords are scrambled with bcrypt at twelve rounds. Failed logins are counted, and the account locks after a set number of failures for a set time. Reset creates a random token, stores only its hash, expires it after an hour and allows three requests per hour. Reset and change then update the password and revoke refresh tokens, in one transaction where used.
inputs: User IDs, emails, plain passwords, reset tokens, IP addresses, and the lockout settings MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS and LOCKOUT_MINUTES.
outputs: Stored password hashes and lockout fields, a raw reset token for the caller to email, and success or thrown errors.
risks: The raw reset token must be emailed by the caller, and that email is not sent yet. Unknown emails and known accounts get different results on reset requests, which reveals accounts. Change password revokes every refresh token, including the current device. Only refresh tokens are revoked, so access tokens stay valid until they expire.
debug: For locked accounts, check failedAttempts and lockedUntil on the user row. For reset problems, check the passwordReset rows for expiresAt and usedAt. For settings, check MAX_LOGIN_ATTEMPTS and LOCKOUT_MINUTES. If the settings are missing, the defaults of five tries and fifteen minutes apply silently.
